newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Chronology of major Asia fire disasters since 1993.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of major Asia fire disasters since 1993.

text.p: Below is a list of major fires in Asia since January 1993.
January 6, 1993 - A basement fire which ignited gas tanks at an apartment block in Chongju, South Korea, killed 28.
January 19, 1993 - 33 died in a fire in an unlicensed 24-hour restaurant in Taiwan's capital Taipei.
February 14, 1993 - A fire blamed on workers carrying out welding work ripped through the Linxi department store in Tangshan, China, killing about 80 people.
April 19, 1993 - At least 34 psychiatric patients, many shackled hand and foot, were killed when fire swept through a mental hospital in Nonsan, South Korea.
May 10, 1993 - Over 200 workers were killed after a fire at a toy factory near Bangkok, Thailand.
November 2, 1993 - A fire at a burst petrol pipeline in Uong Bi town, Vietnam, killed 44. Most died as they were trying to steal fuel when the fire started.
November 19, 1993 - Fire in a Sino-Hong Kong joint venture toy factory in southern Shenzhen province, China, killed 87 workers.
November 26, 1993 - Explosions and fire in the explosives workshop of a chemical plant killed 61 workers in central Hunan province, China.
December 13,1993 - Fire swept through the dormitory of a textile factory in Fuzhou, China, killing 61 sleeping women workers.
January 31, 1994 - Twenty-eight people were killed on a Vietnamese bus when it caught fire after a smoker ignited a load of alcohol.
March 31, 1994 - 24 Taiwan tourists were killed in a pleasure boat fire on Qiandao lake on mainland China. The incident soured relations between the two countries.
June 4 1994 - Forty-five people were burned to death when a bus caught fire in southern Pakistan.
June 16, 1994 - A textile plant at Zhuhai, China, burned down and then collapsed. The official death toll was 76, but unofficial reports said at least 200 died.
October 24 1994 - Twenty-nine people were killed when fire engulfed a pleasure boat carrying 132 passengers at Chungju Lake, South Korea.
November 25, 1994 - A fire in a dance hall in Fuxin, China, killed 233 people. Most were killed by smoke inhalation and poisonous fumes.
December 8 1994 - China's deadliest fire in 15 years killed 325 people, 288 of them children, when flames engulfed a cinema hall in the northwestern town of Karamay.
February 16, 1995 - A fire swept through a karaoke parlour in the central Taiwan city of Taichung, killing 64 people. It was the worst fire in Taiwan since 1949.
March 14 1995 - Fire raged through a hotel in Anshan, China, killing about 30 people.
April 6, 1995 - 29 pupils on a spring outing were killed in a forest fire atop Mount Hongqing, China. Negligence by school officials was blamed.
April 24, 1995 - A short circuit led to a fire at a dance hall in Urumqi, Xinjiang province China, which killed 52.
August 21, 1995 - A group of inmates intent on escape set fire to a dormitory at a rehabilitation centre in Yongin, South Korea, killing about 40 locked-in women.
December 23, 1995 - A fire at a school prize-giving in the Indian town of Dabwali killed at least 425 people.
March 19, 1996 - A fire in a Manila disco killed at least 159 people, mostly teenagers celebrating the start of the school holidays.
March 29, 1996 - At least 10 die in a fire in a department store in Bogor, Indonesia. Earlier, the death toll had been put at 78.

November 20, 1996 - Fire in Hong Kong's Nathan Road tourist shopping street turns into a towering inferno, killing 39 people and injuring 81. It was the worst blaze in a building on record in the British colony.
January 25, 1997 - A blaze in a Hong Kong karaoke bar killed 15 people in the Tsimshatsui red light district. Police suspected arson.
February 23, 1997 - At least 200 people were killed in a fire that engulfed a gathering of Hindu worshippers in eastern India.
